attitude.def: A learned feeling and belief about a person, group, object or idea that predisposes a person to respond in a certain way.

stereotype.def: A generalized belief about the members of a group, which may be partly accurate but is often overgeneralized and applied to individuals who do not fit it.

prejudice.def: An unjustified, usually negative attitude toward a group and its members. It involves feelings, beliefs and a tendency to discriminate.

cognitive-load.def: How much of working memory's limited capacity is in use. Under high cognitive load, people have less room to check automatic stereotypes.

implicit-attitude.def: An automatic association, often outside awareness, about a group or object, which can differ from the attitude a person reports. Reaction-time measures of it vary from testing to testing and predict an individual's behavior only weakly.

just-world.def: Just-world phenomenon: the tendency to believe the world is fair, so that people get what they deserve. It can lead to blaming victims.

in-group.def: A group a person identifies with ("us").

out-group.def: A group a person does not identify with ("them").

outgroup-homogeneity.def: Out-group homogeneity: seeing members of other groups as more alike than members of one's own group.

ingroup-bias.def: In-group bias: favoring members of one's own group, even when the group was formed by chance.

ethnocentrism.def: Judging other cultures by the standards of one's own culture, treating one's own as the right or normal way.

belief-perseverance.def: Holding on to a belief even after the evidence that formed it has been discredited.

confirmation-bias.def: The tendency to seek, notice and remember information that supports what one already believes and to overlook information that challenges it.

cognitive-dissonance.def: The discomfort felt when one's actions and attitudes, or two beliefs, clash. People tend to reduce it by changing the attitude, changing the action or adding a justification.
